verdict.rationale: Honeybadger documents Slack and PagerDuty integrations, lets users choose which error events trigger a notification, offers threshold-based Alarms on BadgerQL queries, and provides anomaly detection for error-volume spikes. That covers the core of event-filtered routing with frequency-style thresholds. missing for 10: documented routing by environment and severity, email as an alert channel, affected-user-count thresholds, explicit per-rule new-issue triggers, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an SRE, I can route alerts by project, environment, and severity to Slack, PagerDuty, or email with per-rule thresholds — new issue, frequency spike, affected-user count

citations.quote: You get to choose which error events result in a notification or ticket being created
Alarms combine a BadgerQL query (“count all slow requests in the past five minutes”) with a threshold (“when count is > 2”) and trigger alerts when the query result exceeds the threshold.
Anomaly detection alerts you when a project’s total error volume deviates from its learned baseline
You can generate an integration key for Honeybadger by logging in to PagerDuty then clicking on “Add New Service” and choosing “Honeybadger” as the service type.
